Screen On can now turn itself off. Pick how long it stays on, let it step aside when the battery runs low, and a restart always gives you your own screen timeout back.

## New

- **Auto-off timer.** Choose 15 min, 30 min, 1 hr, 2 hr, or ∞ under **Keep on for**. The dial's gold ticks count down as the time runs out, and the app shows when it will turn off. The Quick Settings tile shows the end time ("Until 5:40 PM"), and in Wake lock mode the notification shows a live countdown. Picking a different length while it's on restarts the timer from now.
- **Turn off on low battery.** On by default. Screen On turns itself off at 15% battery unless the phone is charging. If you turn it on while already below 15%, it waits until the battery has been above 15% before it can turn off.
- **Exact timing (optional).** On Android 12 and newer, Timeout mode needs the "Alarms & reminders" permission for the timer to end on the minute. If it's missing, an **Allow exact timing** link appears; without it the timer may end a few minutes late. Wake lock mode is always on time.

## Fixed

- **Restarting the phone no longer leaves the screen awake.** Before, if you restarted your phone with Timeout mode on, the timeout stayed at its maximum until you opened the app. Now your own timeout is restored as soon as the phone starts. This also works on phones that block apps from running at startup: the app spots the restart the next time you open it or use the tile.

## Download

Get **`screen-on-v1.1.0.apk`** and install it over 1.0.0; your settings are kept. Requires Android 7.0 or newer. Android may offer to scan the app before installing, because it doesn't come from the Play Store. Tap "Scan app" and it will install normally.
